evidence.text: The entry favors an account in which early Western Zhou inscriptions used 老 for both ‘old’ and ‘father’; adding 丂 as a phonetic marker distinguished 考, with the lower 匕 of 老 usually omitted. It also records a competing account: 丂 was an original graph, proposed to depict an axe handle, borrowed for ‘father’, then given 老 as a classifier. The entry says early bronze 丂 used for ‘father’ lends that account support, but judges the 老-based account better able to explain early Western Zhou usage. These are attributed analyses, not settled formation history.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 考

evidence.field: 考; 說文 and 廣韻 entries, lines 158–168
evidence.text: The entry quotes 說文: ‘考，老也。从老省，丂聲’ and gives 苦浩切. Its listed Guangyun categories are 溪 initial, 上 tone, 豪/皓 rhyme, open, first division. This records the traditional lexicographic analysis and a historical pronunciation notation; it does not independently prove the graph’s original formation.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 考

evidence.field: 考; reported bronze and Warring States uses, lines 177–179
evidence.text: The entry reports bronze 考 for ‘father’ in 兮仲鐘 and for ‘consider/estimate’ in 中山王鼎; it also reports use for 孝 in 孟姬脂𣪕, and readings as 巧 and 孝 in named Warring States bamboo texts. Its discussion says father often refers to a deceased father but not invariably. These source-reported examples support distinct uses; they do not establish a semantic development from ‘father’ to ‘examine’ or date the earliest instance of each sense. The artifacts were not independently inspected here.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 考

evidence.field: 丂; proposed graphic origin and uses, lines 108–112
evidence.text: The entry attributes to 屈萬里 an analysis of oracle-bone and bronze 丂 as a branch form and as the pictographic initial of 柯; it says 屈萬里 earlier followed 說文’s axe-handle interpretation, later revising it to branch. It reports oracle-bone use as a place name, bronze use for ‘father’ and 孝, and Warring States use read as 巧. The referent and original name/pronunciation of the depicted object remain disputed; the page does not establish an axe-handle name that independently explains the loan.

evidence.field: 考; reading and form references, lines 17–32, 118–126
evidence.text: The Taiwan Ministry of Education entry gives Mandarin kǎo and lists 丂 and 攷 among forms classed as variants of 考. It quotes the Shuowen analysis for 考 and records 苦浩切 under 集韻. This supports current Mandarin reading and the dictionary’s variant classification, but not a full chronology of when 考 and 攷 overlapped.

gaps: Official Unicode Unihan pages for U+8003 and U+4E02 failed to open in this invocation. Therefore no current kMandarin claim is offered as externally verified here. The prior dossier reports local kǎo rows for both, but those remain local validation data, not external evidence.

The previous local Baxter–Sagart rows report 丂 *C.qʰˤuʔ and 考 *k-r̥ˤuʔ, with Middle Chinese khawX for both; those distinct Old Chinese forms were not independently verified against an inspected external page in this invocation. Do not collapse them into a single reconstruction or infer phonetic correspondence from modern readings alone.

The exact dates of the cited inscriptions and bamboo manuscripts were not given on the inspected pages, and no primary editions or artifact images were inspected. The earliest attestation of each sense remains unresolved.

The proposed branch, staff, and axe-handle interpretations of 丂 conflict. The actual original object name and pronunciation are not independently established, so an object-name-based loan explanation remains unverified.
Although the inspected dictionary reports 考 for both ‘father’ and ‘consider/estimate’, it does not establish the semantic bridge or a chronology from the kinship sense to ‘examine/test’.
The separate Shuowen analysis for 攷 (攴 plus phonetic 丂), and the historical timing of its overlap with 考, were not investigated in this invocation.
No reuse terms were checked for the CUHK database; findings are concise paraphrases tied to its character-specific pages.
